examples.knowledge_point: Simplifying an Expression by Factoring and Using the Pythagorean Identity
examples.worked_solution:
First, we factor $\sin^2\theta$ from the expression:

$$
\sin^4{\theta}+\sin^2{\theta}\cos^2{\theta} = \sin^2{\theta}\cdot(\sin^2{\theta}+\cos^2{\theta})
$$

Then, we use $\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta = 1$ to simplify the expression in the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot ({sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}) & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot 1={sin}^{2}⁡\theta \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\sin^4{\theta}+\sin^2{\theta}\cos^2{\theta} = \sin^2\theta.
$$

First, we expand the parentheses:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }({sin}^{3}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) & =\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {sin}^{3}⁡\theta +\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }\cdot {cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{3}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta } \\  & =\frac{{sin}^{2}⁡\theta \cdot \cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}+\frac{{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }}{\cancel{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }} \\  & ={sin}^{2}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta  \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that, in the last step, we simplified the right-hand side using ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1.$ 

Therefore, we conclude that

$$
\frac{1}{\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta }({sin}^{3}⁡\theta +{cos}^{2}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )=1.
$$
